description: We are AI students at FPT University with strong interests in deep learning, data preprocessing, and analysis. Our passion lies in creating innovative architectures to solve real-world problems. The 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge is a great opportunity for us to showcase our skills, apply knowledge to practical challenges, and pursue our goal of contributing impactful AI solutions.
summary: In NASA Space Artifact Explorer, young explorers aged 10 to 14 become Night-Shift Communications Operators aboard the guide craft Echo, flying through a three-tier 3D solar system to awaken 17 silent NASA spacecraft resting where their missions ended. Rather than forgotten scrap metal, each machine holds a "Legacy Spark" passed on to future explorers. On the Moon, Surveyor 3 proved the ground could support a lander so Apollo 11’s Eagle descent stage could touch down, Apollo 12’s ALSEP listened for moonquakes, and the Apollo 15 Lunar Rover gave astronauts wheels to travel farther. On Mars, Viking 1 and 2 took the first surface photos, rovers Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity uncovered evidence of ancient water, Phoenix touched subsurface ice, InSight measured marsquakes, and Ingenuity completed 72 flights before resting at Valinor Hills. In Deep Space, Pioneer 10 and 11, NEAR Shoemaker, Dawn, and Kepler extended humanity’s reach to asteroids, giant planets, and over 2,600 exoplanets. By collecting source-verified NASA facts into a Memory Journal and chatting with AI personas bounded by their real final-contact dates, kids discover that every silent spacecraft is a stepping stone to tomorrow.
details:
1. What Does the Project Do & How Does It Work?

NASA Space Artifact Explorer is an interactive 3D web experience designed for young explorers aged 10–14 under the "Abandoned, But Not Forgotten" challenge. Players step into two connected roles: a Night-Shift Communications Operator and an astronaut aboard the fictional guide craft Echo.

The application works through a three-tier 3D architecture:

  • Tier 1 – Solar System Overview: Explores the Sun, planets, moons, and 5 deep-space missions (Pioneer 10, Pioneer 11, NEAR Shoemaker at Eros, Dawn at Ceres, and Kepler) set against an authentic NASA SVS Gaia DR2 / Hipparcos HDR starfield.
  • Tier 2 – Planetary Surface Globes (Moon & Mars): Interactive 3D globes and surface mission maps pinpointing 4 lunar artifacts (Surveyor 3, Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Apollo 12 ALSEP, Apollo 15 LRV) and 8 Martian artifacts (Viking 1, Viking 2, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity) using verified planetary coordinates.
  • Tier 3 – Artifact Inspection, Fact Cards & Grounded AI Chat: Visitors inspect NASA 3D models and archival photos, listen to browser-synthesized character voice introductions, collect source-verified Fact Cards into their Memory Journal & Space Passport, and converse with AI storytelling personas (Surveyor 3, Viking 1, Opportunity).

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Reframing "Space Junk" as Scientific Heritage: Instead of viewing inactive hardware as forgotten debris, children discover how every mission passed a "Legacy Spark" to the next generation—from Surveyor 3 testing lunar soil for Apollo 11, to Apollo 12’s seismometer inspiring InSight on Mars.
  • Combating AI Hallucinations in STEM Education: Every factual claim in our app is tied to a specific factId and verified NASA source (NSSDCA / NASA Science). Kids learn critical media literacy: always check primary scientific sources.

3. Creativity & Innovation

  • The "Memory Cutoff" Narrative Mechanic: Each AI spacecraft persona only knows history up to its real-world final contact date (e.g., June 10, 2018 for Opportunity). When asked about events after its mission ended, the robot admits its memory stops there and invites the child to explore newer missions (InSight, Ingenuity) to find out what happened next.
  • Guided "Legacy Voyage" UFO Tours: Alongside free exploration, the onboard guide Echo leads three structured story chapters (The Moon, Mars, Deep Space) with synchronized camera flights, Web Speech API character voices, and collectible mission stamps.
  • Server-Verified Grounded Chat: Our backend (api/chat.ts & server/llm.ts) filters facts by memoryCutoff and cross-checks every citation and number returned by the LLM against approved NASA records before displaying an answer.

4. Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber), and Drei (@react-three/drei).
  • Audio & Accessibility: Native Browser Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesis) with custom voice profiles, mute/replay controls, and full text fallbacks.
  • Backend & Deployment: Node.js + TypeScript serverless functions on Vercel, with a multi-provider LLM adapter supporting both live LLM APIs and a deterministic offline/mock mode (LLM_PROVIDER=mock) backed by verified fixtures.
  • Data & 3D Assets: Unmodified GLB models and planetary textures from NASA 3D Resources, NASA SVS (CGI Moon Kit, Deep Star Maps 2020, Black Hole visualization), NASA NSSDCA, and attributed open-source community models (Project Apollo NASSP, OldSchool3D, Dan CC BY 4.0).
